data.narrative:
Normal Computing is a Series B chip company founded by Matthias Tan and Faris Sbahi that has raised $75.5M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductor players (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage peers in chips and semiconductors, including SambaNova Systems ($11.0B Series A), d-Matrix ($2.0B Series C), Positron AI ($1.0B Series B), and DEEPX ($529M Series C).

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using the $75.5M raised as a proxy for Series B value, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B progression, yielding $143M. Peer-median analysis across the four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces a median valuation of $1.5B, though the range spans $529M to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot be applied; the sector median P/S is 21.0x across the three public comps, but the target's revenue is not disclosed.

The triangulated valuation range is $122M (low) to $1.7B (high), with a median of $822M across the two applicable methods. The wide dispersion reflects substantive heterogeneity in the peer set—particularly the $11.0B outlier in SambaNova—and the absence of revenue visibility. Key uncertainties are target margins, capital efficiency, and whether the company's technical approach commands a premium or discount to this peer cohort.
